summary: VERDICT: YES -- TClosure DOES support the (R_Υ) internalization; the falsifier did NOT fire and leg A's first real obstacle is CLEARED, mechanized sorry-free. (□E)/(◇I) are the only NIK rules with a relational premise and both range over TClosure 𝒯 G.R; NIK never reads G.X. So (R_χ) reduces to closure absorption: TClosure.absorb_addEdge + NIK.weakenCl (a strict generalization of NIK.weaken to the closure order) give NIK.geomInternalize, instantiated for all three TS5 axioms (refl/symm/trans) and lifted to Deriv. Deriv/Context.le chain closure confirmed adequate. REQUIREMENT-3 VERDICT: NO -- not load-bearing for the quantifier-free {T,B,Four}. PDF p.91 verbatim makes requirement 3 an 'only if' whose subject is 'each of the witness variables in v_χz̄', and p.72's normal form makes v_χz̄ the EMPTY vector when ȳ is empty. It is vacuously true at TS5, so Conflict 7's adjudication is CONFIRMED and Phase 18's deletion removed nothing leg A needs -- do not reverse it. HOWEVER the pre-gate found a SEPARATE, unanticipated blocker: TPrime TS5 Atom is UNINHABITED (tPrime_TS5_false, IsEmpty instance, mechanized). clModel : ClassicalModel 𝒯 G.R quantifies type-wide (.T => ∀ x, R x x), but PDF p.94 makes H ⊨_CL 𝒯 satisfaction IN THE STRUCTURE H with domain = H's underlying set; clModel .T + Graph.edge_mem force G.X = univ, contradicting Context.coinfinite. Root cause is χ_T alone (only TS5 axiom with n=0 premises); {χ_B,χ_4} is harmless. This is a repairable STATEMENT-LEVEL transcription defect, not a mathematical obstruction, and it does NOT block Phase 21: at 𝒯 = ∅ clause 0 is vacuous, so plan v3's D2 '𝒯 = ∅ first' sequencing is independently vindicated. Route remains alive; proceed to Phase 21.
